title: "Exercise · Define a capsule"

Two short, guided exercises against the adopted v0.1 capsule
contract. Complete them before moving on to the [Lab](lab.qmd).

See the [Open Engineering Language Server (OELS) onboarding guide](../../../../oels.qmd)
for the local install and editor setup.

{{< include ../../../../shared/includes/oels.qmd >}}


## Setup

Both exercises read fixtures from the upstream pinned commit
`bf071c2c1b57`. The shared
[Greeting Capsule lab](../../../../labs/greeting-capsule/)'s
`solution/fetch-upstream.sh` downloads what the walkthrough needs
into `labs/greeting-capsule/build/upstream/`. For a one-off, you
can instead `curl` each fixture referenced below from
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/bf071c2c1b57/<path>`
into `/tmp/`.

## Exercise 1 — Classify six upstream fixtures

Below are six fixtures from the upstream conformance set at
`bf071c2c1b57`. Three validate against
[`capsule.schema.json`](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/blob/bf071c2c1b57/capsule.schema.json);
three do not. **Before** running the validator, decide for each
fixture whether it is **valid** or **invalid**, and — if invalid —
which rule it violates. Use the memo1 §1 required-field table and
the memo2 §2 D2 / §3 D3 rules reproduced in the
[lesson](index.qmd#required-and-optional-fields-at-v01).

### The six fixtures (classify first)

1. [`fixtures/valid/greeting.yaml`](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/blob/bf071c2c1b57/fixtures/valid/greeting.yaml)
   — `oe.greeting` worked example from memo1 §3.
2. [`fixtures/valid/github-issue-create.yaml`](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/blob/bf071c2c1b57/fixtures/valid/github-issue-create.yaml)
   — three-segment identifier `github.issue.create`, version `1.4.2`.
3. [`fixtures/valid/pico-state-set.yaml`](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/blob/bf071c2c1b57/fixtures/valid/pico-state-set.yaml)
   — `pico.state.set`, version `0.2.0`, with a non-empty
   `spec.dependencies` carrying a caret pin.
4. [`fixtures/invalid/missing-outputs.yaml`](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/blob/bf071c2c1b57/fixtures/invalid/missing-outputs.yaml)
   — a capsule with `spec.capability`, `spec.inputs`, and
   `spec.dependencies` but **no** `spec.outputs` key.
5. [`fixtures/invalid/version-not-semver.yaml`](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/blob/bf071c2c1b57/fixtures/invalid/version-not-semver.yaml)
   — `metadata.version: "1.0"`.
6. [`fixtures/invalid/capability-upper-case.yaml`](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/blob/bf071c2c1b57/fixtures/invalid/capability-upper-case.yaml)
   — `spec.capability: Greeting`.

Write your classification down (one line per fixture: *valid* or
*invalid, violates memo§…*) before you look at the next section.

### Check with the validator

Run the one-liner from the lab walkthrough against each fixture
(adjust the paths for your `/tmp/` download):

```bash
python3 -c 'import json, yaml, jsonschema, sys; \
jsonschema.validate(yaml.safe_load(open(sys.argv[1])), \
json.load(open("build/upstream/capsule.schema.json"))); print("valid")' \
  build/upstream/fixtures/valid/greeting.yaml
```

Repeat for each file. Valid documents print `valid`; invalid
documents raise `jsonschema.exceptions.ValidationError` with a
message that lines up with the `# fails:` comment at the top of
each `invalid/*.yaml`.

### Worked answer

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Show worked answer"}

| Fixture | Verdict | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `valid/greeting.yaml` | valid | All memo1 §1 required fields present; `oe.greeting` matches memo2 §3 D3 grammar; `0.1.0` is valid SemVer 2.0.0. |
| `valid/github-issue-create.yaml` | valid | `github.issue.create` is three D3 segments; `1.4.2` is valid SemVer; required field set complete. |
| `valid/pico-state-set.yaml` | valid | `pico.state.set` matches D3; `pico.state.lock@0.2.0` in `spec.dependencies` is a valid memo2 §2 D2 caret requirement. |
| `invalid/missing-outputs.yaml` | invalid | memo1 §1 — `spec.outputs` is required (may be `{}` but must be present). |
| `invalid/version-not-semver.yaml` | invalid | memo2 §2 D2 — `metadata.version: "1.0"` is not valid SemVer 2.0.0 (missing patch component). |
| `invalid/capability-upper-case.yaml` | invalid | memo2 §3 D3 — identifier starts with an upper-case letter and has only one segment. |

:::

## Exercise 2 — Version `oe.greeting` using the D2 table

Start from the `oe.greeting` capsule at version `0.1.0` (the memo1
§3 worked example reproduced in the
[lesson](index.qmd#a-valid-minimal-capsule)).

### Step A — Tighten to `0.2.0` by adding an optional input

Add a new input named `locale` that is **not** required, keeping the
existing `value` input and the existing `greeting` output unchanged.
Bump `metadata.version` from `0.1.0` to `0.2.0`. The resulting
capsule is:

```yaml
apiVersion: open-engineering.io/v1alpha1
kind: Capsule
metadata:
  name: greeting
  version: 0.2.0
spec:
  capability: oe.greeting
  inputs:
    value:
      type: string
      required: true
    locale:
      type: string
  outputs:
    greeting:
      type: string
  dependencies: []
```

**Why is this a minor bump?** The row **"Add an optional
`spec.inputs` entry (with no `required: true`)"** in the memo2 §2
D2 breaking-change table is classified **Compatible / minor**.
Existing consumers still satisfy the contract because every
previously-required input is still required, no existing input or
output type changed, and the new input is omitted-by-default.

### Step B — Remove the `greeting` output

Starting from the `0.2.0` capsule in Step A, remove the `greeting`
output entry entirely (leave `spec.outputs: {}`).

**Why is this a major bump?** The row **"Remove a declared
`spec.outputs` entry"** is classified **Breaking / major**. Any
Pico or caller that read `greeting` from the previous contract no
longer sees it, so the next version MUST be `1.0.0`, not `0.3.0`.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Show the two post-change versions"}

- Step A — version `0.2.0`, `oe.greeting` with required `value`,
  optional `locale`, output `greeting`.
- Step B (building on A) — version `1.0.0`, `oe.greeting` with
  required `value`, optional `locale`, outputs `{}`.

:::
